rv.q: Directed by the Tony winner Anna D. Shapiro with minimal fuss and sharp focus, it makes for an incisive and captivating evening.
It is a slow burn of a show, worthy of your attention.
Are You Now or Have You Ever Been remains a powerful distillation of an historical record of a shameful time in American history.

With performances this engaging, Shapiro doesn’t need to do much to make history come alive, and yet her occasionally frenetic pacing betrays a fear that audiences will tune out from what is essentially a C-SPAN highlights reel.
Director Anna D. Shapiro’s star-stacked revival offers much to admire.
Spectators who know or care relatively little about the last century may find the play to be a static, talky experience despite the excellent performances and staging.
There is great power to this alarming revival, which serves as a warning to all of us who love our country and what it has stood for.

cn.t: Critics praise this riveting revival of Eric Bentley's 1972 docudrama about HUAC hearings as alarmingly relevant and electrifying, with Anna D. Shapiro's direction bringing history to powerful, contemporary life through verbatim testimony.
